# Optimal Site Generator Distribution

**Data Sources: Vodacom data, localized for the Cape Town and some surrounding areas**

#### Problem Statement

Load shedding and insecure power supply put a strain on network servicing sites, affecting coverage and availability of those sites with material impact on site revenue generation from user traffic flows. Running generators at sites impacted by power disruptions offers the immediate solution to ensuring sites continue to run during interrupted power supply; however, there is a limited supply of generators that can be deployed to sites, as well as the cost associated with the deployment and running of the generators. Vodacom would like to develop a strategy for the optimal distribution of generators to important sites with the minimum cost attached whilst ensuring coverage needs and availability are maintained.

Key Definitions:

-   Atoll Site ID: Identifier for a physical structure that houses antennas, transmitters, receivers, and networking hardware needed to transmit and receive voice, data, and internet signals. These have a set coverage shape that defines the span of the site's coverage over a physical space (word this better and add refrence)

-   Site Availability: The percentage of time that a specific telecom site, including its radio equipment, power supplies, backhaul, and virtual or physical connection links, is fully operational and capable of processing traffic. (<https://medium.com/>@saeedfelegari/site-availability-in-telecom-metrics-architecture-and-the-real-requirements-behind-the-numbers-37cf574ba711.

    -   This metric is measured as the percentage number of seconds a site is operational over the total number of seconds in a month, with 100%= full availability.

# Section 1: Deterministic MLP Formulation

The generator deployment problem lends itself to the set covering formulation. In this case, we would like to deploy generators the minimum number of sites (and the associated cost) subject to the constraint is \>=95% and at least 90% of total subscribers at full peak/availability can access the network during times of load shedding.

To necessitate this, a few key assumptions have to made:

-   Each site can get only one generator. All cells for each technology (2G,3G,4G,5G) are fully powered by said generator on the site.

-   The cost associated with running a generator is entirely captured by the fuel cost, thus transportation costs are disregarded for now as the generator is deployed once at a site, if that site is chosen. \* get the average cost of fueling and running a mobile generator for n hours

-   We model for Stage 1 load shedding schedule with at most 1 power outage per day for 2hrs .Load shedding affects all sites at the same time. Load shedding happens at peak hours/demand across sites.

-   Average site coverage perimeter=4.24KM, and these site coverage overlap if they are withing this distance of each other. This Site $j$ can serve the subscribers of site $i$ if $d_{ij} \le R$, were R=4.24KM. A site always covers itself.

-   Subscriber location. All subscribers of site $i$ are treated as located at site $i$, so they are either entirely within reach of a powered site or not. This assumes concentrated subscriber densities.

-   Subscribers can connect coverage/network of neighboring sites fluidly (if they are within the average site perimeter). Thus is if one site goes one, and another site within the overlap radius has a generator, then the a subscriber within that radius can access the generator-ran site's network/coverage with no signal degradation at site edges.

-   Unlimited absorption. A powered site can absorb all subscribers of every site within its radius, with no capacity limit.

-   Peak demand. $w_i$ is the subscriber count at site $i$ at full peak. Coverage target. At least 90% of total peak subscribers must be served during the outage.

What I need: Coverage matrix to get the distances between sites.

## Partial Set Covering Formulation

### Sets and parameters

$$
\begin{aligned}
I &: \text{set of sites, indexed by } i, j \\
d_{ij} &: \text{distance between sites } i \text{ and } j \text{ (km)} \\
R &: \text{coverage perimeter (km)} \\
a_{ij} &=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } d_{ij} \le R \quad (\text{so } a_{ii} = 1) \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases} \\
w_i &: \text{peak unique subscribers at site } i \\
\beta &= 0.90 : \text{minimum fraction of total subscribers that must be served}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Decision variables

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_j &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if a generator is deployed at site } j \\
y_i &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if the subscribers of site } i \text{ are served during the outage}
\end{aligned}
$$

### Model

Minimize the number of generators deployed:

$$
\min \sum_{j \in I} x_j
$$ {#eq-obj}

subject to

$$
y_i \le \sum_{j \in I} a_{ij}\, x_j \qquad \forall i \in I
$$ {#eq-cover}

$$
\sum_{i \in I} w_i\, y_i \ge \beta \sum_{i \in I} w_i
$$ {#eq-target}

$$
x_j \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_i \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall i, j \in I
$$ {#eq-domain}

```{r,matrix_set_up,eval=T,echo=F}

#Neighbourhood matrix of sites (symmetric) that only populates 1 if two sites are within R/perimeter distance of each other- thus they overlap and 0 otherwise



# only use site that we have complete sub information for
sites=st_as_sf(inner_join(site_gdf,st_drop_geometry(site_ranges_gdf),by='atoll_site_id'), crs = 4326) %>% select(atoll_site_id)
sites=unique(sites)

dist_matrix =st_distance(sites) 
dist_matrix=as.matrix(units::set_units(dist_matrix, "km"))


# apply neighbourhood condition
r=mean(cpt_site_ranges_gdf$perimeter)
R=units::set_units(round(r,2),'km')

neigh_mat=ifelse(dist_matrix<= R,1,0)

# matrix(neigh_mat,nrow=)
dim(neigh_mat)

 # Check if matrix is symmetrix
isSymmetric(neigh_mat)

# sub cov matrix= diag matrix
# A sub at site i can only access site service if a generator is at its home site or neigboring site

y_mat=matrix(0,nrow=dim(neigh_mat)[1] ,ncol=dim(neigh_mat)[2])
diag(y_mat)=1

# 1st matrix constraint
constraint_1=y_mat-neigh_mat
dim(constraint_1)

# constrint 2, vector to append at the end of const 1
# avg uniq sub at each site

sub_coeff=st_drop_geometry(cpt_site_ranges_subs_gdf) %>% select(avg_nr_unique_subs) %>% pull()

constraint_2=matrix(sub_coeff,nrow=1,ncol=dim(constraint_1)[2])

# check dim
#dim(rbind(constaint_1,constraint_2))

# constrain values
beta=0.9

# total subs covered at full capacity
total_subs=st_drop_geometry(cpt_site_ranges_subs_gdf)  %>% summarise(total_unique_subs=sum(avg_nr_unique_subs)) %>% pull()

# RHS of constrain 1
rhs_1=matrix(rep(0, dim(constraint_1)[2]),nrow=dim(constraint_1)[1],ncol=1)

# RHS of constrain 2
rhs_2=matrix(beta*total_subs,ncol=1,nrow=1)



```

```{r,solve_LP, echo=F, eval=T}

obj_vec=rep(1,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_subs_gdf)) # xi


constraint_mat_lp=rbind(constraint_1,constraint_2)

my_types = rep("B",length(obj_vec)) # enforces boolean output!
rhs_=rbind(rhs_1,rhs_2)
dir_vec=c(rep('<=',dim(constraint_1)[1]),'>=')

# Enter into solver


lp_soln=Rglpk_solve_LP(obj = obj_vec, mat =constraint_mat_lp , types = my_types,dir = dir_vec, rhs = rhs_, max = FALSE) # minimization problm


# Yay!




```

```{r,soln_plot,eval=T,echo=F}

# get indicies

cpt_site_ranges_subs_gdf$gets_gen=lp_soln$solution



# Now map whic sites got a generator
leaflet(cpt_site_ranges_subs_gdf) |> 
  addTiles() |> 
  setView(lng = 18.42322, lat = -33.92584, zoom = 12) |> 
  addPolygons(
    color = "black",
    weight = 1,

    fillColor = ~ifelse(gets_gen == 1, "blue", "white"),

    popup = ~paste0(
      "Site: ", atoll_site_id,
      "<br>Gets generator: ", gets_gen,

    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = c("blue", "white"),
    labels = c("Gets generator ", "No generator "),
    title = "Generator Allocation",
    opacity = 0.9
  )
```

# Section 2: Deterministic MOLP Formulation- Incorporating Revenue-led Site Importance

Naturally, the choice to deploy a generator at a site is not only determined by cost alone, but by the relative importance of the site in terms of its traffic flows and revenue. Thus an additional objective to the problem would be to minimize (or at least preserve) aggregate peak traffic flow loss across sites and thus minimize (at least preserve) peak revenue loss at these sites.

For simplicity's sake (and available data), we assume the following, in addition to the key assumptions in Section 1:

-   Revenue at a site,$Rev_i$, is a monotonically increasing function of traffic. Thus, a relatively high-revenue site implies that a high-traffic site.

-   As such, only the revenue objective is added to the initial generator minimization problem. We aim to minimize the loss of revenue at these sites

-   The average monthly site revenues are generated at peak times across sites. The sum of these across sites would ideally be preserved or maximised.

-   **Revenue follows the subscriber:** The traffic/revenue that would be ordinarily attributed to a site before loadshedding, can be "absorbed" into neighboring sites by virtue of the subscribers still being able to access neigbouring sites that have generators as assumed in Section 1.

-   Site rankings are derived from the normalized revenue of each site. Thus the goal would be minimize the sum of ranks(?)

-   We initially assume that revenue preservation and generator cost minimization are weighted equally: $w1=w2=0.5$

### Additional parameters

Let $R_i$ denote the revenue of network site $i \in I$. Normalise each KPI to $[0,1]$:

$$
\tilde{Rev}_i = \frac{Rev_i - \min_k Rev_k}{\max_k Rev_k - \min_k Rev_k},
\qquad
$$

The composite importance score of site $i$ is

$$
s_i = rank(R_{i})\
st.\max(s_i)= \sum(x_i) 
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_i &: \text{average monthly peak revenue at site } i \\
\rho_i &= r_i \Big/ \textstyle\sum_{k \in I} r_k : \text{normalized revenue (importance weight)} \\
G &: \text{target (budget) number of generators} \\
\gamma &: \text{target fraction of total peak revenue preserved} \\
\omega_1, \omega_2 &: \text{goal weights}, \; \omega_1 + \omega_2 = 1 \\
d_G^{+} &\ge 0 : \text{generators deployed above target } G \\
d_r^{-} &\ge 0 : \text{shortfall of preserved revenue below target } \gamma \textstyle\sum_i r_i
\end{aligned}
$$

#### Weighted Archimedian Formulation

$$
\min \;\; \omega_1 \frac{d_G^{+}}{G} \;+\; \omega_2 \frac{d_r^{-}}{\gamma \sum_{i \in I} r_i}
$$ {#eq-gp-obj}

subject to the original constraints

$$
y_i \le \sum_{j \in I} a_{ij}\, x_j \qquad \forall i \in I
$$ {#eq-gp-cover}

$$
\sum_{i \in I} w_i\, y_i \ge \beta \sum_{i \in I} w_i
$$ {#eq-gp-target}

and the two goal constraints

$$
\sum_{j \in I} x_j - d_G^{+} \le G
$$ {#eq-gp-goal-gen}

$$
\sum_{i \in I} r_i\, y_i + d_r^{-} \ge \gamma \sum_{i \in I} r_i
$$ {#eq-gp-goal-rev}

$$
x_j \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_i \in [0,1], \quad d_G^{+}, d_r^{-} \ge 0
$$ {#eq-gp-domain}

Where $G$ is the initial optimal solution from the LP formulation in Section 1.


For the above simulation the goal constrains are defined as:\

```{r,goal_set_up, eval=T, echo=FALSE,include=F}

#
w1=0.5
w2=0.5
gamma=0.95 # 1-gamma=revenue loss percentage, gamma is the lease rev that we want to preserve

# normalize revenue
cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf$rev_norm = (cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf$monthly_rev - min(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf$monthly_rev , na.rm = TRUE)) / 
                  (max(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf$monthly_rev , na.rm = TRUE) - min(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf$monthly_rev , na.rm = TRUE))


tot_rev=st_drop_geometry(unique(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf)) %>% summarize(sum(rev_norm)) %>% pull() # Total avg monthly revenue thant we want to preserve


# we want to preserve the normalized revenue
G2=gamma*tot_rev

# Let G1 be the optimum number of generators that were determined from Section 1

G1=lp_soln$optimum # total number of generators
G1

```

#### Archimedian Set up and Solution

```{r,mogp_set_up_arch, eval=T,echo=F ,include=F}

# order of obj (dg,dr,x1,x2,....,xn, y1,y2,....yn) yi is the revenue that is still preserved at a site if it either got a generator OR that ,xi s ite
xn_coeff=rep(0,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf))
yn_coeff=rep(0,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf))
dg_coeff=w1/G1
dr_coeff=w2/G2


# obj vector 
obj_vec_ac=c(dg_coeff,dr_coeff,xn_coeff,yn_coeff);length(obj_vec_ac)

# Goal Constraints
g1_constraints=matrix(c(-1,0, rep(1,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf) ),rep(0,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf) )),ncol=length(obj_vec_ac),nrow=1)


rev_coeff=st_drop_geometry(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf) %>% select(rev_norm) %>% pull()

rev_coeff_g2_2=matrix(rev_coeff,nrow=1,ncol=length(rev_coeff)) # coeff of yi in G2 constraint

# In 

xn_coeff_g2_2=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf))


dg_coeff_g2_2=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1) # coeff of dg in G2 constraint

dr_coeff_g2_2=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1) # coeff of dr in G2 constraint

g2_constraint=cbind(0,dr_coeff_g2_2,xn_coeff_g2_2,rev_coeff_g2_2);dim(g2_constraint)


# Hard Constraints from Section 1, extended to include yi and dg and dr
dg_coeff_hrd_const=matrix(0,nrow=dim(neigh_mat)[1],ncol=1)
dr_coeff_hrd_const=matrix(0,nrow=dim(neigh_mat)[1],ncol=1)

a1=cbind(dg_coeff_hrd_const,dr_coeff_hrd_const,-1*neigh_mat,y_mat) # expanded hard constraint matrix 1

# dim(a1)[2];length(obj_vec_ac)cbind(rep(0,length(xn_coeff)),dg_coeff_hrd_const,dr_coeff_hrd_const,-1*neigh_mat,y_mat)


# Expanded hard constraint 2

dg_coeff_hrd_const2=matrix(0,ncol=1,nrow=1)
dr_coeff_hrd_const2=matrix(0,ncol=1,nrow=1)

yi_coeff_hrd_const2=matrix(sub_coeff,nrow=1,ncol=length(yn_coeff)) # coeff of yi in second hard constraint
xi_coeff_hrd_const2=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=length(yn_coeff)) # coeff of xi in second hard constraint

dim(dg_coeff_hrd_const2)[2];dim(dr_coeff_hrd_const2)[2];dim(
yi_coeff_hrd_const2)[2];dim(xi_coeff_hrd_const2)[2]

# expanded second hard constraint matrix
a2=cbind(dg_coeff_hrd_const2,dr_coeff_hrd_const2,xi_coeff_hrd_const2,yi_coeff_hrd_const2)


```

```{r,mogp_arch_soln, eval=T,echo=F ,include=F}


obj_vec_ac=c(dg_coeff,dr_coeff,xn_coeff,yn_coeff)

constraint_mat_arc=rbind(g1_constraints,g2_constraint,a1,a2); dim(constraint_mat_arc)

my_types_b = rep("B",(  length(xn_coeff)+(length(yn_coeff) ))) # enforces boolean output for xi, yi!
my_types_c = rep("C",1) # continuous output for dr
my_types_i = rep("I",1) # integer output for dg

my_types_ar=c(my_types_i,my_types_c,my_types_b );length(my_types_ar)


rhs_=rbind(matrix(G1,nrow=1,ncol=1),  matrix(G2,nrow=1,ncol=1),rhs_1,rhs_2)
dir_vec=c('<=','>=',rep('<=',dim(constraint_1)[1]),'>=');length(dir_vec)

# Enter into solver


mogp_arc_soln=Rglpk_solve_LP(obj = obj_vec_ac, mat =constraint_mat_arc , types = my_types_ar,dir = dir_vec, rhs = rhs_, max = FALSE) # minimization problm

 mogp_arc_soln # Interprete tomorrow
```

#### Chebyshev Formulation

$$
\lambda \ge 0 : \text{maximum weighted normalized deviation across the goals}
$$

### Model

$$
\min max(w_1d^+_G,w_2d^-_r)=D
$$ {#eq-ch-obj}

subject to the original constraints

$$
y_i \le \sum_{j \in I} a_{ij}\, x_j \qquad \forall i \in I
$$ {#eq-ch-cover}

$$
\sum_{i \in I} w_i\, y_i \ge \beta \sum_{i \in I} w_i
$$ {#eq-ch-target}

the goal constraints

$$
\sum_{j \in I} x_j - d_G^{+} \le G
$$ {#eq-ch-goal-gen}

$$
\sum_{i \in I} r_i\, y_i + d_r^{-} \ge \gamma \sum_{i \in I} r_i
$$ {#eq-ch-goal-rev}

the Chebyshev (minimax) constraints

$$
\omega_1 \frac{d_G^{+}}{G} \le D
$$ {#eq-ch-max-gen}

$$
\omega_2 \frac{d_r^{-}}{\gamma \sum_{i \in I} r_i} \le D
$$ {#eq-ch-max-rev}

and the domain constraints

$$
x_j \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_i \in [0,1], \quad d_G^{+}, d_r^{-},D \ge 0
$$ {#eq-ch-domain}

```{r,cb_set_up,eval=T,echo=F}

# order of obj (D,dg,dr,x1,x2,....,xn, y1,y2,....yn) yi is the revenue that is still preserved at a site if it either got a generator OR that ,xi s ite
D_coeff=1
dg_coeff=0
dr_coeff=0
xn_coeff=rep(0,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf))
yn_coeff=rep(0,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf))




# obj vector 
obj_vec_cb=c(D_coeff,dg_coeff,dr_coeff,xn_coeff,yn_coeff);length(obj_vec_cb)

# Goal Constraints
g1_constraints_cb=matrix(c(0,-1,0, rep(1,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf) ),rep(0,nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf) )),ncol=length(obj_vec_cb),nrow=1);dim(g1_constraints_cb)[2]


rev_coeff=st_drop_geometry(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf) %>% select(rev_norm) %>% pull()

rev_coeff_g2_2=matrix(rev_coeff,nrow=1,ncol=length(rev_coeff)) # coeff of yi in G2 constraint

# In 

xn_coeff_g2_2=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=nrow(cpt_site_ranges_rev_gdf))


dg_coeff_g2_2=matrix(0,nrow=1,ncol=1) # coeff of dg in G2 constraint
```

# Section 3: Simulated Annealing Formulation\*

To apply simulated annealing on the initial LP formulation, the constrained optimization problem is transformed to its Langrangian representation which essentially incorporates the constraints of the LP problem into the objective function that will be minimized.

## Lagrangian formulations of the set covering problem

### Assumptions

\begin{enumerate}
\item The candidate generator locations coincide with the demand sites $I$,
and $a_{ii} = 1$ (a generator covers its own site).
\item Coverage is binary and deterministic: $a_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$.
\item Weights $w_i \ge 0$ are fixed, and $0 < \beta \le 1$ is the required covered fraction of $W = \sum_{i \in I} w_i$.
\item For fixed $\mathbf{x}$ the best choice is $y_i = \min\{1, \sum_{j} a_{ij} x_j\}$,
so $y$ can be eliminated: $C(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i \in I} w_i\, \mathbb{1}\{\sum_{j} a_{ij} x_j \ge 1\}$.
\end{enumerate}

### Original problem

$$
z^{*} = \min \sum_{j \in I} x_j
\quad \text{s.t.} \quad
y_i \le \sum_{j \in I} a_{ij} x_j \;\; \forall i, \quad
\sum_{i \in I} w_i y_i \ge \beta W, \quad
x_j, y_i \in \{0,1\}.
$$

### Formulation 1: relax the coverage target (multiplier $\lambda \ge 0$)

$$
g_1(\lambda) = \lambda \beta W + \min_{\mathbf{x} \in \{0,1\}^{I}}
\Big\{ \sum_{j \in I} x_j - \lambda\, C(\mathbf{x}) \Big\}
\;\le\; z^{*}.
$$

The inner problem is a prize-collecting covering problem and is solved by simulated annealing.

### Formulation 2: relax the linking constraints (multipliers $\mu_i \ge 0$)

$$
g_2(\boldsymbol{\mu}) = \sum_{j \in I} \min\Big\{0,\; 1 - \sum_{i \in I} a_{ij} \mu_i\Big\}
+ \min_{\mathbf{y} \in \{0,1\}^{I}} \Big\{ \sum_{i \in I} \mu_i y_i \;:\; \sum_{i \in I} w_i y_i \ge \beta W \Big\}
\;\le\; z^{*}.
$$

The problem separates into independent decisions on $x_j$ and a knapsack-cover problem in $y$. Maximise $g_2$ over $\boldsymbol{\mu} \ge 0$ by subgradient steps, giving a lower bound.

### Penalised objective used by simulated annealing

$$
F_{\lambda}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j \in I} x_j + \lambda \max\{0,\; \beta W - C(\mathbf{x})\}.
$$

If $w_i$ are positive integers and the target is $\lceil \beta W \rceil$, any $\lambda > 1$ makes every minimiser of $F_{\lambda}$ feasible.

```{r}
# Solving the above

# =============================================================================
# Simulated annealing for generator placement (penalised Lagrangian objective)
#
#   F(x) = sum_j x_j + lambda * max(0, beta*W - C(x))
#
#   x_j  = 1 if a generator is placed at site j
#   C(x) = total weight of sites covered by at least one placed generator
#   W    = total weight, beta = required covered fraction
#
# Same building blocks as the SA examples: initial solution, evaluate, perturb,
# geometric cooling, accept/reject.
# =============================================================================

set.seed(100)   # for repeatability

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data  (REPLACE THIS BLOCK WITH YOUR OWN)
#    A : n x n 0/1 coverage matrix, A[i, j] = 1 if site i is in the coverage
#        polygon of a generator at j (set the diagonal to 1)
#    w : weight of each site (area, population, importance score, ...)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
n   <- 60
pts <- cbind(runif(n), runif(n))
A   <- (as.matrix(dist(pts)) <= 0.22) * 1
diag(A) <- 1
w   <- rep(1, n)

beta   <- 0.90                 # required covered fraction
W      <- sum(w)
target <- beta * W             # (use ceiling(beta * W) if weights are integers)

# Penalty weight. lambda > 1 / min(w) makes every minimiser of F feasible,
# because covering one uncovered site then always pays for the generator.
lambda <- 2 / min(w[w > 0])

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Evaluation function
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
covered_weight <- function(x){
  covered <- as.vector(A %*% x) >= 1
  sum(w[covered])
}

evaluate_x <- function(x){
  shortfall <- max(0, target - covered_weight(x))
  sum(x) + lambda * shortfall
}

is_feasible <- function(x){
  covered_weight(x) >= target - 1e-9
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Initial solution
#    Random placement. A good starting point helps: you could instead start
#    from a greedy solution or from all sites (always feasible).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
get_initial_x <- function(n){
  rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Perturbation: flip one site, or swap a placed and an unplaced generator
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
perturb_x <- function(x){
  ones  <- which(x == 1)
  zeros <- which(x == 0)

  if(runif(1) < 0.5 || length(ones) == 0 || length(zeros) == 0){
    # flip a random site
    j <- sample.int(length(x), 1)
    x[j] <- 1 - x[j]
  } else {
    # swap: move one generator to a currently unplaced site
    j <- ones[sample.int(length(ones), 1)]
    k <- zeros[sample.int(length(zeros), 1)]
    x[j] <- 0
    x[k] <- 1
  }
  return(x)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Repair: drop redundant generators while the target stays met
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
repair_x <- function(x){
  repeat{
    ones <- which(x == 1)
    if(length(ones) == 0) break
    cov_without <- sapply(ones, function(j){
      y <- x
      y[j] <- 0
      covered_weight(y)
    })
    ok <- cov_without >= target - 1e-9
    if(!any(ok)) break
    j <- ones[ok][which.max(cov_without[ok])]   # remove the least useful one
    x[j] <- 0
  }
  return(x)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Simulated annealing
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
start_temp  <- 5
temp_factor <- 0.9995
n_iter      <- 20000

cur_x  <- get_initial_x(n)
cur_fx <- evaluate_x(cur_x)

# results (pre-allocated, as storing every solution gets slow for large n)
all_fx   <- numeric(n_iter)
all_ngen <- numeric(n_iter)
all_feas <- logical(n_iter)

best_x <- NULL            # best FEASIBLE solution seen (fewest generators)

for(i in 1:n_iter){

  # generate a candidate solution
  prop_x <- perturb_x(cur_x)

  # evaluate the candidate solution
  prop_fx <- evaluate_x(prop_x)

  # calculate the probability of accepting the candidate
  anneal_temp <- start_temp * temp_factor ^ i
  accept_prob <- exp(-(prop_fx - cur_fx) / anneal_temp)

  # accept or reject the candidate
  if(prop_fx < cur_fx){
    cur_x  <- prop_x
    cur_fx <- prop_fx
  } else {
    if(runif(1) < accept_prob){
      cur_x  <- prop_x
      cur_fx <- prop_fx
    }
  }

  # keep the best feasible solution (fewest generators)
  if(is_feasible(cur_x) && (is.null(best_x) || sum(cur_x) < sum(best_x))){
    best_x <- cur_x
  }

  # store results
  all_fx[i]   <- cur_fx
  all_ngen[i] <- sum(cur_x)
  all_feas[i] <- is_feasible(cur_x)
}

if(is.null(best_x)){
  stop("No feasible solution found: increase n_iter, start_temp or lambda.")
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
best_x <- repair_x(best_x)

cat("Generators placed       :", sum(best_x), "\n")
cat("Covered weight fraction :", round(covered_weight(best_x) / W, 4),
    "(target", beta, ")\n")
cat("Selected sites          :", which(best_x == 1), "\n")

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
plot(all_fx, type = "l", xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Penalised objective F(x)")
plot(all_ngen, type = "l", xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Generators in current solution")
plot(1:n_iter, start_temp * temp_factor ^ (1:n_iter), type = "l",
     xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Temperature")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

```

### Properties

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Weak duality:} $g_1(\lambda) \le z^{*}$ and $g_2(\boldsymbol{\mu}) \le z^{*}$ for all multipliers $\ge 0$.
\item \textbf{Duality gap:} the problem is integer, so $\max_{\lambda} g_1$ and $\max_{\boldsymbol{\mu}} g_2$ can be strictly below $z^{*}$.
\item \textbf{Role of SA:} it supplies a feasible upper bound $\sum_j x_j^{\text{best}}$, and the
Lagrangian supplies the lower bound, giving a reportable gap.
\end{itemize}

# Section 4:Discrete Event Simulation for Stochastic Load Shedding Scheduling

What is different:\
One of my key assumptions initial LP formulation is that the load shedding schedule is deterministic and that all sites are experience power outages at the same time. In reality this is not the case.

There is a stochastic element to the prevalence of the power outages and as such not all sites will experiance interrupted power at the same time and require generators. In light of this, the problem is formulated as a discrete event and run simulations based on the appropriate statistical distributions of the loadshedding event.

Key Assumptions:

-   The loadshedding stage for a given day is stochastic and as such follows an appropriate statistical distribution, however, the actual load shedding times that come as a result of that announced stage are deterministic and follow a set schedule.

-   Only a percetange of sites are affected by load shedding at the same time. The percentage at any given schedule is deterministic.

### Empirical distribution of the weekly stage

Let $s_w \in \{0,1,\dots,8\}$ be the load-shedding stage in week $w$, defined as the most occurring stage over that week in the historical record ($N$ weeks in total, of which $n_k$ were at stage $k$). The stage is sampled from the empirical probability mass function $$
\hat{\pi}_k = \Pr(s_w = k) = \frac{n_k}{N}, \qquad k = 0,1,\dots,8,
\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{8} \hat{\pi}_k = 1,
$$ with no parametric distribution assumed. Sampling uses inverse transform: draw $U \sim \text{Uniform}(0,1)$ and set $$
\sigma_w = \min\Big\{k : \hat{F}(k) \ge U\Big\}, \qquad
\hat{F}(k) = \sum_{m=0}^{k} \hat{\pi}_m .
$$

```{r}

# Frequency of load shedding schedules by week, in 2022 as these were load shedding heavy years

weekly = loadshedding_history_clean %>%
  mutate(week_date = as_date(floor_date(ls_date, "week")),
         stage = as.integer(as.character(stage))) %>%   # factor -> numeric
  filter(year(week_date) == 2022) %>%
  count(week_date, stage, name = "freq") %>%
  arrange(week_date, desc(freq), desc(stage)) %>%       # ties -> higher stage
  group_by(week_date) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()



all_weeks = tibble(week_date = seq(min(weekly$week_date),max(weekly$week_date), by = "week"))

# Replace weeks that have no data with stage 0
weekly_full =all_weeks %>%
  left_join(weekly, by = "week_date") %>%
  mutate(stage = replace_na(stage, 0L))

# Empirical frequency table for SIMUL8
stage_table = weekly_full %>%
  count(stage, name = "n_weeks") %>%
  complete(stage = 0:8, fill = list(n_weeks = 0)) %>%
  mutate(prob = (n_weeks / sum(n_weeks)*100), # probability of that stage 
         cum_prob = cumsum(prob)) # cumulative probability of that stage


stage_table %>%
  filter(n_weeks > 0) %>%
  select(n_weeks, stage,prob,) %>%
  write.table("clipboard", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
    
write_clip(stage_table)
```

```{r}
           num_sites_affected, percentage_affected)

sched %>% count(stage, day_of_month, start_hour) %>% filter(n > 1)  # should be empty

# 2. Expected % of sites off at a random moment, by stage and day of month

  group_by(stage, day_of_month) %>%
  mutate(stage=factor(stage, level=ls_levels)) %>% 
  summarise(pct_day = sum(percentage_affected * duration) / 24, .groups = "drop") %>%
  bind_rows(expand_grid(stage = factor(0), day_of_month = 1:31, pct_day = 0))

# 3. 2022 calendar with actual day of month and week
cal <- tibble(date = seq(as.Date("2022-01-01"), as.Date("2022-12-31"), by = "day")) %>%
  mutate(day_of_month = day(date),
         week_date = as_date(floor_date(date, "week")))

# 4. Weekly average % for every stage in every full week
week_pct <- cal %>%
  crossing(stage = 0:8) %>%
   mutate(stage=factor(stage, level=ls_levels)) %>% 
  left_join(pct_day, by = c("stage", "day_of_month")) %>%
  group_by(week_date, stage) %>%
  summarise(n_days = n(), week_pct = mean(pct_day), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_days == 7)

# 5. Spread per stage: is one number per stage defensible?
stage_pct <- week_pct %>%
  group_by(stage) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct = mean(week_pct), sd_pct = sd(week_pct),
            min_pct = min(week_pct), max_pct = max(week_pct))

# 6. Realised 2022 weeks (join to the weekly stage you built earlier)
realised <- weekly_full %>% 
   mutate(stage=factor(stage, level=ls_levels)) %>% 
left_join(week_pct, by = c("week_date", "stage"));realised
```
